material.notes: AUDIT 19 (matched confirmed, text gap found): own comparer (reference crop template-placed in the committed 1x sheet; flat = 3 x 3 spread of at most 6 levels; glyph zone = text mask or difference from the -notext twin, grown 2 px; off = any channel over 2 levels). Fill, shadow and rim: 0 flat px off outside the sheet's caption row, 0 px over 12 levels outside the glyph zone (36 flat px counted in the glyph zone of the hover cell, state layer pixels under text); the fill spans the same columns as the reference (168 px at my row scan, equal in both) in rest and hover, so the round 37 width fix holds, and a re-render at 48316ea1f is byte for byte the committed sheet. But text ink within 2 levels fell from 99.0 % (before round 37) to 83.9 %: the right aligned shortcut column (x 140 to 160 of the crop) now sits a fraction of a pixel off the reference (218 of its 220 text mask px differ), because the width rounding moved its start; the labels stay at about 99 %. Matched stands on the strict metric and on the precedent of the slider and switch (text 56 to 66 %); md-menu is a real Material Web reference, so the spec-written cap does not apply. | ROUND 37 (review back to matched, audit 18 downgrade answered): the menu fill was 167.6 wide after the round 35 text widths and was painted on the fraction; Blink lays the box out on the pixel grid, so the width is now rounded to whole pixels (137 px, the reference). Strict scripts/material/cmp.py menu: off 0, ring 0, shadow 0, rim 0 in light and dark. | ROUND 37 (restated): Android text follows the Chrome-on-Windows DirectWrite model (93 to 96 percent of ink exact; a second mode, AndroidSkia, exists beside ChromeWin) and the references are Chrome for Testing on Windows with greyscale text, not Linux Chromium. Older notes below that describe another text model are history. | AUDIT 18 (matched to review, answered): own comparer (tm2.py: reference crop trimmed to the component plus 6 px, template-placed in the committed 1x sheet by the pixels outside the text mask and then by the whole crop; flat = 3 x 3 spread of at most 6 levels, ink margin 2 px). Text ink within 2 levels: 99.0 % light, 99.5 % dark, flat px off 0 in both, so round 35 text did make the glyphs exact. But the menu box lost a pixel: light: the menu fill is 136 px wide against the reference 137 (md-menu-rest), so the right edge column is off in all 301 rows, 301 px over 12 levels per cell (0 at audit 17); the shadow tail beside it is the same 306 rows over 2 levels as before. The same comparer on the sheets of audit 17 (113b678bf) gives 0, so the round 35 line and width change caused it, and no other Android control changed outside its text. A shape error over the full height of the menu is not a rounding difference; one column of width fixes it. | ROUND 31 (review to matched): the Search row's text and shortcut sat 4 px off because the row put its 16 dp gap on both sides of the filler and so overflowed the menu; md-menu-item's gaps are now paddings. The gallery's star and plus placeholders for Settings and Refresh are replaced by the settings, refresh and image Material Icons paths that matglyph.e draws and the references re-captured. Flat px off 26 to 0 and with glyphs 228 to 18 (light and dark, rest and hover). | Compared with Material Web (docs/ui/looks/ref/material) in Chromium with greyscale text; strict metric of scripts/material/cmp.py (reference flat px off beyond the ink margin, ring px over 12 levels). Round 31: Roboto is placed on a whole baseline and fitted vertically (x-height rounded up from a 0.375 fraction, cap height, ascender and descender to whole rows), Android profile only. ROUND 37: the text edge percentages and 'not pixel equal' findings above predate the round 35 DirectWrite model and are superseded by the last gap. The menu width is now snapped to the pixel grid as Blink paints it (overlay.menu_panel), so the right edge column is exact again.
gaps: The shortcut column is a fraction of a pixel off the reference since round 37 (text ink within 2 levels 83.9 % light; the labels about 99 %): keep the shortcut text on the fractional start it had before the width was rounded
Rows are 56 dp, as md-menu draws them (the M3 spec says 48)

Text follows the Chrome-on-Windows DirectWrite model of android-text.md (hinted outline, six by five samples, ClearType boxes averaged to grey, Skia's pre-blend table), which is how the Chrome for Testing on Windows references are drawn: 93 to 96 % of text ink pixels are exact (every channel within 2 levels) on the Material sheets, the rest are anti-aliasing edges of single glyphs. A second mode, AndroidSkia (a device's Skia over FreeType), exists next to it for Android devices; no device capture exists to measure it against.
